headline: Committee reviews building costs and wildfire debris site land

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: The committee reviewed a $1.5 million request for the 60 South Church Street building and a $4 million wildfire debris site land purchase.
meeting.recap: One testifier asked why the wildfire debris site is called "permanent.".[[0:07:10]] The committee voted eight ayes to send pending bills to the Council Chair for the next term.[[0:09:13]] The building is planned to hold the county IT division, the MIMA headquarters and an emergency operations center.[[0:13:08]] The capital projects coordinator said permits, equipment wait times and a federal grant review caused delays.[[0:13:50]] He estimated a shortfall of about $1.5 million to finish construction by the end of next year.[[0:15:44]] He said the county expects to move in around July or August 2025.[[0:36:39]] The county is asking for $4 million to buy two parcels for a permanent wildfire debris disposal site.[[1:06:07]] The managing director said the county dropped eminent domain, a court process to take land, for a different parcel.[[1:10:21]] Officials said speed matters so the county does not lose federal help with debris work.[[1:17:53]]
meeting.next: The county is working with state and federal partners on an alternate truck route for moving debris. Officials said they will tell the Council when a closing date for the temporary debris site is known.

moments.q: Floors sag as much as two and a half inches

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: The county plans to spend $4 million on two parcels for a permanent wildfire debris disposal site.
issues.why: Officials said losing federal help would mean the county pays for and runs the debris work itself.

deadlines.d: towards the middle to early middle part of the year, of next year
deadlines.t: Permanent disposal site ready for use.

issues.next: Officials hope to have the permanent site ready in the early-to-middle part of next year.
issues.brief: The parcel called unit three, where the permanent site will go, costs $2,477,550.[[#1]] An official said commercial debris removal is about 99% complete.[[#2]] The managing director said there is no plan to mix everyday trash with the Lahaina debris.[[#3]] Moving debris from the temporary site to the permanent site is expected to be reimbursable while the federal mission continues.[[#4]]
